title: How to Reduce Risks of Bad Air Quality
titleZh: 如何降低空气质量差带来的风险
credits: Aniruddha Ghosal reported on this story for the Associated Press. John Russell adapted it for VOA Learning English.

sentences.en: Air quality differs from place to place and day to day.
sentences.zh: 空气质量因地区而异，也随日期变化。

sentences.en: But about 99 percent of the world’s population breathes air at some point that does not meet pollution guidelines set by the World Health Organization (WHO).
sentences.zh: 然而，全球约99%的人口在某些时候呼吸的空气达不到世界卫生组织（WHO）设定的污染标准。

sentences.en: Different forms of air pollution kill about 7 million people each year, the U.N. health agency estimates.
sentences.zh: 联合国卫生机构估计，各种形式的空气污染每年约导致700万人死亡。

sentences.en: But health experts say there are some actions individuals can take to protect themselves, even in the world’s most polluted cities.
sentences.zh: 但健康专家表示，即使在全球污染最严重的城市，个人也能采取一些措施来保护自己。

sentences.en: The first step is to start with the understanding that air is not only polluted when it looks smoky or smoggy, said Tanushree Ganguly.
sentences.zh: 第一步是首先要认识到，空气并不只是在看起来烟雾弥漫或有雾霾时才被污染，图什里·甘古利说。

sentences.en: She is an air quality expert with the Energy Policy Institute of Chicago’s India program.
sentences.zh: 她是芝加哥能源政策研究所印度项目的空气质量专家。

sentences.en: “Blue skies can’t guarantee you clean air,” Ganguly told The Associated Press.
sentences.zh: "蓝天并不能保证你呼吸到清洁的空气，"甘古利告诉美联社。

sentences.en: Air pollutants often come from people burning things.
sentences.zh: 空气污染物通常来自人们燃烧各种物质。

sentences.en: Examples include fuels as well as clearing operations involving crops or trees.
sentences.zh: 例子包括燃料，以及涉及作物或树木的清理作业。

sentences.en: Pollutants can also be released from wildfires.
sentences.zh: 污染物也可能从野火中释放出来。

sentences.en: Among the most dangerous particles we can breathe in are called particulate matter.
sentences.zh: 我们能够吸入的最危险的颗粒物之一被称为颗粒物。

sentences.en: The smallest of these are known as PM 2.5.
sentences.zh: 其中最小的被称为PM2.5。

sentences.en: This is because they are less than 2.5 microns in diameter.
sentences.zh: 这是因为它们的直径小于2.5微米。

sentences.en: These particles can travel deep inside human lungs and are mostly created by burning fuels.
sentences.zh: 这些颗粒物能深入人体肺部，主要由燃烧燃料产生。

sentences.en: Larger particles, known as PM 10, are linked to agriculture, roadways, mining or wind-blown dust.
sentences.zh: 较大的颗粒物被称为PM10，与农业、道路、采矿或风吹扬尘有关。

sentences.en: Other dangerous pollutants include gases like nitrogen dioxide or sulfur dioxide, which are also produced from burning fuels.
sentences.zh: 其他危险的污染物还包括二氧化氮或二氧化硫等气体，它们也来自燃烧燃料。

sentences.en: This information comes from Anumita Roychowdhury, an air pollution expert at the Center for Science and Environment in New Delhi.
sentences.zh: 这些信息来自新德里的科学与环境中心的空气污染专家阿努米塔·罗伊乔杜里。

sentences.en: The American-based Health Effects Institute says air pollution is the second-largest risk factor for early death worldwide, behind high blood pressure.
sentences.zh: 总部位于美国的健康影响研究所表示，空气污染是全球范围内导致早死的第二大风险因素，仅次于高血压。

sentences.en: Short-term exposure can cause asthma attacks and increase the risk of heart attacks and stroke, especially in older people and those with existing medical problems.
sentences.zh: 短期暴露可能引发哮喘发作，并增加心脏病发作和中风的风险，尤其在老年人和已有疾病的人群中更为明显。

sentences.en: Long-term exposure can cause serious heart and lung problems that can lead to death.
sentences.zh: 长期暴露可能导致严重的心脏和肺部问题，进而危及生命。

sentences.en: A recent study by the U.N. children’s agency UNICEF found that more than 500 million children in East Asia and Pacific countries breathe unhealthy air.
sentences.zh: 联合国儿童基金会UNICEF最近一项研究发现，东亚和太平洋地区有超过5亿儿童在不洁净的空气中呼吸。

sentences.en: The pollution is linked to the deaths of 100 children under age 5 every day.
sentences.zh: 这种污染与每天100名5岁以下儿童的死亡有关。

sentences.en: June Kunugi, UNICEF’s Regional Director for East Asia, said the polluted air limits growth, harms lungs and affects thinking abilities.
sentences.zh: 联合国儿童基金会东亚地区主任June Kunugi表示，受污染的空气会限制发育、损害肺部并影响思维能力。

sentences.en: “Every breath matters, but for too many children every breath can bring harm,” she said.
sentences.zh: 她说：'每一次呼吸都很重要，但对太多儿童来说，每一次呼吸都可能带来伤害。'

sentences.en: Over 6,000 cities in 117 countries now record and follow air quality levels.
sentences.zh: 如今，117个国家的6000多座城市都在记录并追踪空气质量水平。

sentences.en: Many mobile apps include air quality information as well.
sentences.zh: 许多手机应用也纳入了空气质量信息。

sentences.en: But it can be difficult to know how bad the air is by looking at these numbers.
sentences.zh: 但仅凭这些数字，往往难以判断空气究竟有多糟糕。

sentences.en: To help people better understand air quality levels, many countries have established an air quality index, or AQI.
sentences.zh: 为了帮助人们更好地了解空气质量水平，许多国家设立了空气质量指数，即AQI。

sentences.en: Larger numbers on this index mean worse air.
sentences.zh: 这一指数上的数字越大，意味着空气质量越差。

sentences.en: Different countries have different air quality standards.
sentences.zh: 不同国家有不同的空气质量标准。

sentences.en: For example, India’s daily PM 2.5 limit is more than 1.5 times higher than in Thailand and 4 times higher than WHO standards.
sentences.zh: 例如，印度的每日PM2.5限值比泰国高出1.5倍以上，比世界卫生组织的标准高出4倍。

sentences.en: For individuals, experts say the goal should be to limit exposure when air quality is bad, by staying indoors or wearing a mask.
sentences.zh: 专家表示，对个人而言，目标应当是在空气质量差时尽量减少暴露，比如待在室内或佩戴口罩。

sentences.en: This is not always possible, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，这并不总是可行的。

sentences.en: Danny Djarum is with the World Resources Institute.
sentences.zh: Danny Djarum在世界资源研究所工作。

sentences.en: He told the AP there are many people who live or work outside and “can’t really afford” to stay indoors.
sentences.zh: 他告诉美联社，有许多人或生活在户外，或在外工作，'根本无法负担'待在室内。

sentences.en: People also need to watch indoor air pollution that can be caused by common household activities like cooking or burning incense.
sentences.zh: 人们还需要关注室内空气污染，这可能由烹饪或焚烧香等常见家庭活动造成。

sentences.en: While air purifiers can help reduce indoor air pollution, experts say they do have limitations.
sentences.zh: 专家表示，空气净化器虽有助于减少室内空气污染，但确实存在局限。

sentences.en: The devices work by pulling air from a room and then pushing it through a filter that traps pollutants.
sentences.zh: 这些设备的工作原理是从室内抽取空气，再将其通过过滤网，从而截留污染物。

sentences.en: The filtered air is then sent back into the room.
sentences.zh: 过滤后的空气随后被送回室内。

sentences.en: Air purifiers work best when used in small spaces and when people are nearby.
sentences.zh: 当在狭小空间中使用且附近有人的时，空气净化器的效果最佳。

sentences.en: This is because they can only clean a certain amount of air, said Rajasekhar Balasubramanian of the National University of Singapore.
sentences.zh: 新加坡国立大学的拉贾塞卡哈尔·巴拉苏布拉马尼安表示，这是因为空气净化器只能净化一定量的空气。

sentences.en: He added, “If we have a tiny air purifier in a large room, it won’t be effective.”
sentences.zh: 他补充道：'如果在一个大房间里放一台小小的空气净化器，它就不会有效果。'

sentences.en: I’m John Russell.
sentences.zh: 我是约翰·拉塞尔。

sentences.en: And I'm Caty Weaver.
sentences.zh: 我是凯蒂·韦弗。
